records.proposedFallText: Persian conquest ended the Saite dynasty in 525 BCE. Native dynasties recovered control from 404 to 343 BCE, followed by renewed Persian rule until Alexander took Egypt in 332 BCE.
records.dateBasis: Phases within a continuing cultural history; not one continuous sovereign state.

records.finding: Imported end at 323 BCE excludes the Meroitic phase. Aksum existed alongside later Kush; a campaign is not proof of automatic state succession. Sixth-century Nubian political heirs include Nobatia, Makuria and Alodia.
records.safeAction: Remove unqualified successors=[aksum] and exact fell footer; preserve campaign as attributed, approximately dated event pending specialist review.
records.chronology: Napatan/Meroitic kingdom broadly first millennium BCE through fourth century CE. Do not turn archaeological period limits into exact founding/fall years.
records.remaining: Read inscription translation and recent Meroitic archaeological synthesis; distinguish Kerma, Napata and Meroe; match later Nubian IDs before links.
records.sourceConflict: LOC Sudan says destruction about350; LOC Ethiopia says conquest/abandonment around300. These incompatible secondary dates must not be averaged or converted into an exact event. The accessible original inscription opening confirms Noba campaign but not exact Meroe destruction.

records.finding: UNESCO describes kingdom first to eighth centuries, while introduction refers to tenth-century political decline and later coronations. Neither supports exact fall 940 or immediate Zagwe takeover.
records.safeAction: Remove predecessor Kush and unverified fell object. Mark lifetime chronology unresolved; preserve map observation coverage separately.
records.remaining: Specialist late Aksum chronology and Zagwe transition, not a linear Kush-Aksum-Zagwe chain.
records.additionalFinding: Older LOC Ethiopia study explicitly describes extended decline into the twelfth century and a post-Aksumite kingdom before Zagwe accession about1137. This independently rejects immediate Zagwe succession at940; it does not license a new exact year.

records.finding: Imported split at 200 BCE is map observation segmentation, not creation of a new civilization. Canonical shared dossier should preserve both IDs as aliases or period routes. Roman Carthage is a later political context.
records.safeAction: Set terminal Punic limit -146 on later carthage record; consolidate identity before expanding earlier carthaginian-empire coverage.
